claim.value: Exports already active at the transition should remain a distinct comparison group.
claim.scope: Cohort comparisons organized by queue-entry time and exposure to the concurrency step.

provenance.rationale: P020 explicitly requires retaining exports active at the transition as a distinct group within these cohort comparisons.

signal_basis.value: The concurrency limit is lowered after a baseline, while active exports continue to completion. Actual concurrency can adjust gradually as work drains, so comparisons track queue-entry time and exposure to the step, distinguishing exports already active at the transition.
signal_basis.scope: Scheduled exports in the tested canary pool across the concurrency transition.

provenance.rationale: These spans establish the scheduled workload, controlled step, continuation of active work, potentially gradual adjustment, and exposure-based cohort comparison.
The bounded comparison rule is directly warranted; no unresolved empirical relation is needed.

rationale: Exports active at the transition have pre-step operating history and potentially mixed exposure during adjustment. Keeping them distinct preserves that relevant exposure difference when comparing responses to the concurrency step.
uncertainty: Distinct grouping does not itself ensure comparable workloads or uniform exposure within the group; neither is required by this claim.
